\chapter{A First Three-Place Map}
\label{ch:gu-first-three-places}
\hlchaptermodality{24}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can hear, say, read, and write market, home, and temple in Gujarati.}

Seven one-atom lessons keep meaning ahead of print, isolate the one required consonant, then score all three words in listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[bajār]{\gu{બજાર} — hear market first}

\label{lesson:GU-C20-hear-bajar}



\begin{quote}
Listen twice: \textbf{bajār}. It means \textbf{market}. Do not study the Gujarati spelling yet; hold only the sound and meaning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Point to a market picture when you hear \emph{bajār}, then say \emph{bajār} once from the English cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bajār]{\gu{બજાર} — market on the page}

\label{lesson:GU-C20-bajar}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{bajār} from the meaning \textbf{market}. Now look:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{બજાર}} — \emph{bajār} — market
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\gu{બજાર}} once, then copy it once while naming the sound \emph{bajār}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://gu.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%AA\%B5\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8B\%E0\%AA\%B6:\%E0\%AA\%B6\%E0\%AA\%AC\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%A6\_\%E0\%AA\%85\%E0\%AA\%A8\%E0\%AB\%81\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%B0\%E0\%AA\%AE\%E0\%AA\%A3\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BE}{Gujarati Wiktionary word index}.

\section[ghar]{\gu{ઘર} — hear home first}

\label{lesson:GU-C20-hear-ghar}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{bajār} for market. Now listen twice: \textbf{ghar} means \textbf{home} or \textbf{house}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Choose home or market as you hear \emph{ghar} and \emph{bajār}. Then say \emph{ghar} once from the meaning cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://gu.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%AA\%98\%E0\%AA\%B0}{\gu{ઘર} — Gujarati Wiktionary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[gha]{\gu{ઘ} — one consonant for gh}

\label{lesson:GU-W20-gha}



\begin{quote}
The consonant \textbf{\gu{ઘ}} begins \emph{ghar}. Today it is only a sound and writing shape; the complete word waits for the next lesson.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Watch the model, trace \textbf{\gu{ઘ}} twice, and copy it once while saying \emph{gha}.

\section[ghar]{\gu{ઘર} — home on the page}

\label{lesson:GU-C20-ghar}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{ઘર}} — \emph{ghar} — home; house
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[bajār — ghar — mandir]{Three places in four skills}

\label{lesson:GU-C20-places-three}



\begin{quote}
Say market, home, and temple from their meaning cues.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
